# obot_mcp_access_rule (Resource)

Manages one policy shown under MCP Servers > Access Policies. Supports importing existing rules, including Everything. Policies grant access additively: deleting this rule leaves other grants in effect. This resource does not manage vMCP profiles. See the [catalog and access-policy guide](../guides/catalogs-and-access-policies.md) for adopting and removing Everything.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "obot_mcp_access_rule" "administrators" {
  display_name = "Administrator MCP access"
  subjects = [{
    type = "obotGroup"
    id   = "admin"
  }]
  resources = [{
    type = "selector"
    id   = "*"
  }]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `display_name` (String) The policy's display name, for example `Everything`. The name does not determine its subjects or grants.
- `resources` (Attributes Set) Targets receiving the grant: `mcpServerCatalogEntry`, `mcpServer`, or `selector` with ID `*` (everything). Referenced entries and servers must belong to `catalog_id`. An empty set grants no access. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resources))
- `subjects` (Attributes Set) Subjects receiving access: `user` (Obot user ID), `group` (identity-provider group ID), `obotGroup` (Obot built-in group ID), or `selector` with ID `*` (everyone). An empty set grants no access. Preserve actual subjects when importing; a rule named Everything need not grant everyone access. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--subjects))

### Optional

- `catalog_id` (String) The catalog containing this policy. Defaults to `default`. Changing it replaces the rule.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The Obot access-control rule identifier.

<a id="nestedatt--resources"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resources`

Required:

- `id` (String) Referenced object or group ID. A `selector` must use `*`.
- `type` (String) Reference type. See the parent attribute for supported types.


<a id="nestedatt--subjects"></a>
### Nested Schema for `subjects`

Required:

- `id` (String) Referenced object or group ID. A `selector` must use `*`.
- `type` (String) Reference type. See the parent attribute for supported types.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# The destination resource must match the existing policy's definition.
import {
  to = obot_mcp_access_rule.administrators
  id = "default/acr1-everything"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import obot_mcp_access_rule.administrators default/acr1-everything
```
